A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HSfM research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary materials support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: V1 reports original HSfM evaluations on EgoHumans and EgoExo4D, ablations, re-identification analysis, and qualitative reconstructions.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and reports revised EgoExo4D results in Table 2.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 retain the same initialization, human-based scale recovery, two-stage optimization, and human and scene objectives. The new mention of potentially using BEV for non-standard body sizes does not establish an implemented method change.

E1.justification: Both benchmarks and the smartphone demonstrations remain. The stated EgoExo4D coverage narrows: v1 describes using all available cameras, whereas v2 explicitly excludes sequences containing egocentric RGB views. This is a change in reported input-scenario coverage, without establishing exactly which earlier examples were removed.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains UnCaliPose, DUSt3R, MASt3R, and HSfM initialization in the corresponding comparisons. The comparison variants in Tables 3 and S.1 also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section S.4.2 replaces the all-available-camera EgoExo4D description with a filtered RGB evaluation requiring correct re-identification and excluding egocentric RGB sequences. It specifies 182 validation videos instead of approximately 200, retaining one frame per video. This revises the reported protocol; the PDFs do not establish the exact change in sample membership.

E4.justification: The loss-component, human-count, scale-initialization, and camera-count ablations are retained, with identical numerical rows in Tables 3 and S.1. The re-identification analysis also remains. New Figure S.3 provides another view of an already illustrated reconstruction, rather than a distinct analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates for the quantitative evaluations. V2's random-frame sampling description does not introduce repeated-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 2 substantially revises the EgoExo4D comparison: HSfM W-MPJPE changes from 0.56 to 0.50 m, while UnCaliPose changes from 2.90 to 3.59 m and its PA-MPJPE from 0.14 to 1.19 m. The CCA@15 ranking reverses: HSfM versus MASt3R changes from 0.16 versus 0.14 to 0.14 versus 0.17. These are revised results under a revised reported selection, not demonstrated same-setting gains. EgoHumans and ablation-table values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical setup, assumptions, initialization equations, and objectives in Equations 1–10 are unchanged. Correcting supplementary RTA/s-RTA labels to CCA/s-CCA aligns them with existing main-text metrics and introduces no new mathematical definition or proof.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains joint metric-scale reconstruction of humans, scenes, and cameras from sparse uncalibrated images, with mutual reconstruction benefits. Updated numerical summaries do not redefine this contribution or its novelty claim.

C2.justification: V2 acknowledges MASt3R's better EgoExo4D camera-center accuracy and relates weaker scale recovery to using one person. It also newly discusses residual uneven ground and clarifies that noisy human point clouds are not used as human-reconstruction priors. Existing re-identification and initialization limitations remain.

D1.justification: Section S.4.2 adds the complete list of 182 EgoExo4D take/frame pairs and specifies random frame selection. Section S.5 newly identifies the first four-camera frames of EgoHumans tagging and basketball sequences used for hyperparameter tuning. The optimizer, learning rate, minimum optimization steps, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds MONSt3R as a cited route toward extending the work to videos. The existing related-work coverage and positioning against human reconstruction and SfM methods otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 condenses method and experimental prose, removes the separate Evaluation subsection heading, and moves the in-the-wild demonstration narrative into Section S.1. These are localized editorial and structural revisions within the retained overall organization.

P2.justification: V1 Figure 4 becomes v2 Figure S.1, existing supplementary figures are renumbered, and a top-down reconstruction view is added as Figure S.3. Figures and tables are repositioned, including placing Tables 2 and 3 together. Table S.1 corrects RTA/s-RTA column labels to CCA/s-CCA without changing its numerical entries.

improvement.justification: V2 improves reproducibility through exact evaluation frames and tuning details, and better qualifies camera-estimation limitations. However, v1's abstract W-MPJPE baselines agree with Table 2, while v2's abstract gives 3.59 and 3.01 m against table values of 3.51 and 3.59 m; its EgoExo4D results prose also gives UnCaliPose PA-MPJPE as 0.13 m versus 1.19 m in the table. These unresolved inconsistencies in central results offset the documentation benefits, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
